cefr.note: Simulado escrito pela Fisk, com a estrutura e os pesos do MET. Não é uma prova oficial da Michigan Language Assessment: a nota aqui é uma estimativa de treino, e a conversão de acertos para scaled score é aproximada (linear).

bands.desc: Usuário proficiente. Compreende com facilidade discursos e textos longos e complexos.
Usuário independente avançado. Compreende ideias principais e pontos de vista em contextos sociais, profissionais e acadêmicos.
Usuário independente. Compreende os pontos principais de fala e textos claros sobre assuntos familiares.
Usuário básico. Compreende informações essenciais de mensagens curtas, simples e previsíveis.
Abaixo do nível mínimo medido pelo MET nesta seção.

sections.name: Listening · Part 1
sections.instructions: In this part of the test, you will hear short conversations between two people. After each conversation, you will hear a question about it. Choose the best answer to the question. There are 19 questions in Part 1. The conversations and questions will not be repeated.

sections.name: Listening · Part 2
sections.instructions: In this part of the test, you will hear longer conversations between two people. After each conversation, you will answer some questions about it. There are 14 questions in Part 2. The conversations and questions will not be repeated. If you want to, you may take notes as you listen.

sections.name: Listening · Part 3
sections.instructions: In this part, you will hear some short talks. After each talk, you will answer some questions about it. There are 17 questions in Part 3. The talks and questions will not be repeated. If you want to, you may take notes as you listen.

sections.name: Grammar
sections.instructions: This section focuses on your ability to use English grammar. Each question has only one correct answer.

sections.name: Reading
sections.instructions: This section focuses on your ability to understand written English. Read each passage and answer the questions about it.

questions.text: _____ the committee's objections, the proposal moved forward unchanged.
opts: Despite
Although
Even though
Whereas
questions.expl: Depois da lacuna vem um substantivo ("the committee's objections"), e antes de substantivo o contraste se marca com DESPITE (ou in spite of). Although, even though e whereas exigiriam uma oração com sujeito e verbo. Portanto, a resposta correta é DESPITE.

questions.text: The lab repeated the experiment _____ the first set of readings was inconsistent.
opts: because
because of
due to
owing to
questions.expl: Aqui vem uma oração completa ("the first set of readings was inconsistent"), e a causa antes de oração é BECAUSE. Because of, due to e owing to só aparecem antes de substantivo. Portanto, a resposta correta é BECAUSE.

questions.text: Attendance fell every year; _____, the festival was cancelled in 2024.
opts: consequently
nevertheless
meanwhile
besides
questions.expl: O cancelamento é o resultado da queda de público, e CONSEQUENTLY (como therefore, thus, as a result) é o conector de resultado. "Nevertheless" marcaria contraste, que não é o caso. Portanto, a resposta correta é CONSEQUENTLY.

questions.text: The council agreed _____ the decision until the new budget is approved.
opts: to postpone
postponing
to postponing
postpone
questions.expl: O verbo AGREE é seguido de to + infinitivo. "Postponing" seguiria verbos como avoid, consider ou suggest, que pedem gerúndio. Portanto, a resposta correta é TO POSTPONE.

questions.text: Residents objected to _____ charged for a service they never requested.
opts: being
be
have been
been
questions.expl: Em "object to", o "to" é preposição, e depois de preposição o verbo vai para -ing. Como os moradores receberam a cobrança, a forma é passiva: BEING charged. Portanto, a resposta correta é BEING.

questions.text: The auditors will _____ the discrepancy before signing the report.
opts: look into
call off
put off
take up
questions.expl: LOOK INTO é investigar, examinar os fatos de uma situação — que é o que auditores fazem com uma divergência antes de assinar. Portanto, a resposta correta é LOOK INTO.

questions.text: The success of the trial depends _____ how quickly volunteers can be recruited.
opts: on
of
from
in
questions.expl: É DEPEND ON. "Depend of" é um dos erros mais frequentes de falantes avançados e não existe em inglês. Portanto, a resposta correta é ON.

questions.text: Not until the audit was complete _____ the extent of the loss.
opts: did the board realize
the board realized
the board did realize
realized the board
questions.expl: Expressão negativa no início da frase ("not until") exige inversão: o auxiliar vem antes do sujeito, como numa pergunta, e o verbo principal fica na forma base. Portanto, a resposta correta é DID THE BOARD REALIZE.

questions.text: _____ the funding been approved earlier, the clinic would have opened in March.
opts: Had
If
Were
Should
questions.expl: É a condicional sem "if": HAD + sujeito + particípio equivale a "If the funding had been approved". Com "if" a frase precisaria de "had" depois do sujeito. Portanto, a resposta correta é HAD.

questions.text: The dispute was settled between the landlord and _____.
opts: me
I
myself
mine
questions.expl: Depois de preposição entra o pronome objeto. "Between you and I" é o erro mais comum de quem já fala bem, justamente por soar mais formal. Portanto, a resposta correta é ME.

questions.text: There is very little _____ that the policy achieved its aim.
opts: evidence
evidences
an evidence
many evidence
questions.expl: EVIDENCE é incontável em inglês: não tem plural e não aceita artigo indefinido. Por isso vem com "little", e não com "few" ou "many". Portanto, a resposta correta é EVIDENCE.

questions.text: The second prototype performed _____ than the first.
opts: far better
very better
more better
the better
questions.expl: Comparativo se intensifica com far, much ou considerably — nunca com "very". E "better" já é o comparativo de "well", então não leva "more". Portanto, a resposta correta é FAR BETTER.

questions.text: The longer the drought lasted, _____ the harvest became.
opts: the smaller
smaller
the smallest
more small
questions.expl: Na estrutura "the + comparativo… the + comparativo", as duas partes levam THE. "Small" é adjetivo curto, então o comparativo é "smaller". Portanto, a resposta correta é THE SMALLER.

questions.text: The manual does not explain _____ after each use.
opts: how the filter should be cleaned
how should the filter be cleaned
how should be the filter cleaned
the filter how should be cleaned
questions.expl: Pergunta encaixada volta à ordem da afirmativa: sujeito antes do verbo, sem inversão. Depois de "does not explain" não há mais pergunta. Portanto, a resposta correta é HOW THE FILTER SHOULD BE CLEANED.

questions.text: The technicians calibrate the instruments _____.
opts: carefully in the lab every morning
in the lab carefully every morning
every morning carefully in the lab
in the lab every morning carefully
questions.expl: A ordem dos advérbios é modo, lugar e tempo: como (carefully), onde (in the lab) e quando (every morning). Portanto, a resposta correta é CAREFULLY IN THE LAB EVERY MORNING.

questions.text: The committee recommended that the deadline _____ by two weeks.
opts: be extended
is extended
was extended
will be extended
questions.expl: Depois de verbos como recommend, insist e request, a oração com "that" usa o subjuntivo: o verbo fica na forma base, e na passiva isso dá BE + particípio. Portanto, a resposta correta é BE EXTENDED.

questions.text: If the sensor _____ calibrated last week, the readings would be reliable now.
opts: had been
was
were
has been
questions.expl: É um condicional misto: a condição está no passado ("last week") e o resultado, no presente ("now"). A condição pede had + particípio. Portanto, a resposta correta é HAD BEEN.

questions.text: The samples arrived unsealed; someone _____ the container during transport.
opts: must have opened
should have opened
can't have opened
might not have opened
questions.expl: MUST HAVE é a conclusão quase certa sobre o passado, apoiada na evidência — aqui, as amostras terem chegado abertas. Portanto, a resposta correta é MUST HAVE OPENED.

questions.text: By the time the results are published, the team _____ on the project for three years.
opts: will have been working
will work
will be working
has been working
questions.expl: Com "by the time" e uma duração ("for three years"), a forma é o future perfect continuous: a ação começou antes e continua até aquele ponto do futuro. Portanto, a resposta correta é WILL HAVE BEEN WORKING.

questions.text: The researcher _____ findings were questioned has since published a correction.
opts: whose
who
whom
which
questions.expl: WHOSE marca posse dentro da oração relativa: os achados são do pesquisador. "Who" e "whom" não indicam posse, e "which" não se usa para pessoas. Portanto, a resposta correta é WHOSE.

units.title: Passage 1 · Questions 71–75
units.passageIntro: This passage is about why cities are hotter than the countryside around them.
units.passage:
Step out of a park and onto a parking lot on a summer afternoon and you can feel the difference without any instrument. The air above the asphalt is several degrees warmer, and it stays warmer long after the sun has set. Climate scientists call this the urban heat island, and for decades it was treated as a curiosity of city life rather than a problem worth solving.

The mechanism is not complicated. Concrete, brick and asphalt absorb solar radiation during the day and release it slowly at night, while the dark colour of most road surfaces makes them absorb more than they reflect. Trees and soil do the opposite: water evaporating from leaves carries heat away, and a canopy of branches keeps the ground beneath it in shade. A neighbourhood that has replaced its trees with buildings has, in effect, removed its own cooling system.

What has changed is the precision with which the effect can be measured. Satellites now record surface temperature street by street, and in city after city the maps show the same pattern: the hottest districts are the ones with the fewest trees, and those districts tend to be the poorest. In one American study, the gap between the leafiest and the barest neighbourhoods of a single city reached seven degrees Celsius on the same afternoon.

That finding has moved the heat island out of the weather report and into city budgets. Planting a tree is cheap, and unlike an air conditioner it cools the street rather than warming it further. The difficulty is that a sapling planted today will not shade anyone for fifteen years, which is a long time in the life of a city council.

questions.text: Why does the author describe stepping from a park onto a parking lot?
opts: to show that the effect can be noticed without measurement
to argue that parking lots should be removed from cities
to explain how satellites record surface temperature
to compare summer afternoons with summer evenings
questions.expl: A frase diz que a diferença se sente "without any instrument". A cena de abertura serve para mostrar que o fenômeno é perceptível sem medição — e não para criticar estacionamentos ou explicar satélites, que só aparecem mais adiante.

questions.text: According to the passage, how do trees cool the area around them?
opts: by evaporating water from their leaves and shading the ground
by reflecting solar radiation back into the atmosphere
by absorbing heat during the day and releasing it at night
by lowering the temperature of the soil beneath the asphalt
questions.expl: O segundo parágrafo diz exatamente isso: "water evaporating from leaves carries heat away, and a canopy of branches keeps the ground beneath it in shade". Absorver de dia e soltar à noite é o que fazem concreto e asfalto, não as árvores.

questions.text: In the third sentence of paragraph 3, which word is closest in meaning to bare?
opts: having few trees
having little rainfall
having narrow streets
having old buildings
questions.expl: O trecho contrasta "the leafiest" com "the barest" bairros. Se um extremo é o mais arborizado, o outro é o que quase não tem árvore. O contraste dentro da própria frase é que resolve.

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about the districts with the fewest trees?
opts: They are usually inhabited by people with lower incomes.
They were built more recently than the leafier districts.
They are the districts where satellites are least accurate.
They have already begun large tree-planting programmes.
questions.expl: O texto afirma que os bairros mais quentes são os com menos árvores e acrescenta que "those districts tend to be the poorest". A conclusão sobre a renda é sustentada pelo texto, embora ele não fale em renda com todas as letras.

questions.text: According to the last paragraph, what makes tree planting difficult for a city council?
opts: The benefit arrives many years after the cost.
Trees are more expensive than air conditioning.
Saplings do not survive in the hottest districts.
City budgets are decided by national governments.
questions.expl: O último parágrafo diz que plantar é barato, mas que a muda "will not shade anyone for fifteen years, which is a long time in the life of a city council". O obstáculo é o prazo, não o preço — o texto diz o contrário sobre custo.

units.title: Passage 2 · Questions 76–80
units.passageIntro: This passage is about how researchers study the way birds find their way.
units.passage:
Every autumn, millions of songbirds leave northern Europe for Africa, and most of them travel at night. A bird that has never made the journey before will arrive, alone, at a wintering ground it has never seen. How it does so has occupied biologists for more than a century, and the answer has proved to be several answers at once.

The first serious evidence came from a planetarium. In the 1960s, researchers placed captive buntings in a circular cage during the migration season and recorded the direction in which the restless birds tried to escape. When the artificial sky above them was rotated, the birds changed direction accordingly. They were reading the stars — or, more precisely, the point around which the stars appear to turn.

A second line of work pointed somewhere else entirely. Birds fitted with small magnets, or tested inside coils that distorted the magnetic field, lost their sense of direction even under a clear sky. Whatever the mechanism, the planet's magnetic field was clearly part of the system. For a while the two findings were treated as rival explanations, and researchers argued about which sense was the real one.

The argument faded once it became possible to test the two together. Birds deprived of one cue simply relied more heavily on the other, and birds given contradictory information recalibrated overnight, treating the stars as the reference against which the magnetic reading was corrected. The modern view is less tidy than either of the old ones: migration runs on a set of overlapping systems, none of which is indispensable on its own.

questions.text: According to the passage, what did the researchers in the 1960s observe?
opts: The birds changed direction when the artificial sky was rotated.
The birds stopped trying to escape when the stars were hidden.
The birds followed the magnetic field rather than the stars.
The birds were unable to orient themselves inside a cage.
questions.expl: O segundo parágrafo descreve o experimento do planetário: girando o céu artificial, "the birds changed direction accordingly". As outras alternativas trocam esse resultado por outro que o texto não relata.

questions.text: Why does the author mention birds fitted with small magnets?
opts: to introduce evidence for a second navigational sense
to explain why the planetarium experiment was flawed
to describe how birds are tracked on their journey south
to show that captive birds behave differently from wild ones
questions.expl: Os ímãs abrem o parágrafo que apresenta "a second line of work". A menção serve para trazer a evidência do campo magnético, não para desqualificar o experimento anterior.

questions.text: In the last sentence of paragraph 3, what does the word the two findings refer to?
opts: the star compass and the magnetic sense
the magnets and the coils used in the tests
the clear sky and the distorted field
the northern breeding grounds and the wintering grounds
questions.expl: Os dois achados são os dos dois parágrafos anteriores: a orientação pelas estrelas e a orientação pelo campo magnético. Ímãs e bobinas são instrumentos de um mesmo achado, não dois achados.

questions.text: In the last paragraph, which phrase is closest in meaning to recalibrated?
opts: adjusted one system using the other
returned to the place where they started
repeated the journey a second time
lost the ability to orient themselves
questions.expl: A própria frase explica o termo: as aves passaram a tratar as estrelas como referência "against which the magnetic reading was corrected" — ou seja, ajustaram um sistema pelo outro.

questions.text: What is the main point of the passage?
opts: Bird navigation depends on several systems that back one another up.
The planetarium experiments of the 1960s have since been disproved.
The magnetic sense is the only reliable guide over long distances.
Young birds learn the route by following experienced adults.
questions.expl: O texto percorre dois achados, mostra que foram tratados como rivais e fecha dizendo que a migração "runs on a set of overlapping systems, none of which is indispensable on its own". As outras alternativas cobrem só um trecho ou contradizem o texto.

texts.html:
The Riverside Tool Library

Borrow what you need. Return it when you're done.

A tool library works like any other library, except that the shelves hold drills, ladders and sewing machines instead of books. Members pay an annual fee and may borrow up to four items at a time for one week.

  • Over 1,200 tools, from garden shears to tile cutters
  • Annual membership: £30, or £12 for students and pensioners
  • Free repair clinic every second Saturday, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.
  • No experience required — staff will show you how to use anything you borrow

Open Tuesday to Saturday. Membership can be arranged at the counter or online.

Frequently asked questions

Why does the library charge a fee at all?
The fee covers replacement of worn tools and the wages of one part-time technician. It is deliberately kept below the cost of hiring a single power tool for a weekend, so that membership pays for itself on the first visit.

What happens if I break something?
Nothing, in most cases. Ordinary wear is expected and is what the fee is for. We ask only that you report the damage, because a tool returned quietly with a fault will injure the next borrower.

Can I keep an item longer than a week?
Yes, provided nobody is waiting for it. Renewals are made online and take effect immediately; items on the waiting list cannot be renewed.

Five minutes with Nadia Okafor, founder

Where did the idea come from?
From a cupboard. I had bought a tile cutter for one bathroom and used it once in nine years. Multiply that cupboard by every household on the street and you have an enormous amount of metal sitting still.

Was it hard to convince people?
The borrowing was easy to explain. What surprised me was the repair clinic. People arrive with a broken lamp expecting to be told it is beyond saving, and they leave having mended it themselves. That is when they join — not when they borrow, but when they fix.

What would you tell another town?
Start with the shelf you already have. We began with forty tools in a church hall. The building came later, and it came because the members asked for it.

questions.text: According to Text A, how many items may a member borrow at one time?
opts: four
one
twelve
thirty
questions.expl: O texto A diz que os membros "may borrow up to four items at a time for one week". Os outros números aparecem no texto, mas são o preço e o prazo, não a quantidade.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of Text B?
opts: to answer doubts that might stop someone from joining
to advertise the tools that have recently arrived
to explain how the library was originally founded
to warn members about the penalties for late returns
questions.expl: As três perguntas do texto B são objeções típicas de quem hesita — a taxa, o estrago e o prazo. Ele existe para desarmar essas dúvidas. A fundação é assunto do texto C.

questions.text: According to Text B, what should a member do after damaging a tool?
opts: report the damage
pay for a replacement
repair it before returning it
renew the item online
questions.expl: O texto B diz que, na maioria dos casos, nada acontece: "We ask only that you report the damage". Pagar pelo conserto é justamente o que ele diz não ser necessário.

questions.text: What can be inferred from Text B about the annual fee?
opts: It is lower than the cost of renting one power tool for a weekend.
It has risen every year since the library opened.
It is waived for members who volunteer at the repair clinic.
It is the library's only source of income.
questions.expl: O texto diz que a taxa é mantida "below the cost of hiring a single power tool for a weekend". As outras alternativas afirmam coisas que o texto não sustenta.

questions.text: In Text B, which phrase is closest in meaning to ordinary wear?
opts: normal damage from regular use
a fee charged for heavy items
clothing lent with the equipment
the time a tool spends on the shelf
questions.expl: A frase seguinte esclarece: é o que a taxa cobre e o que se espera do uso. "Wear" aqui é o desgaste natural de quem usa a ferramenta.

questions.text: Why does Nadia Okafor mention a cupboard in Text C?
opts: to illustrate how much unused equipment sits in homes
to explain where the first tools were stored
to describe the shelving used in the current building
to complain about the price of a tile cutter
questions.expl: Ela conta que comprou um cortador de azulejo e o usou uma vez em nove anos, e conclui: "Multiply that cupboard by every household". O armário é a imagem do equipamento parado.

questions.text: According to Text C, what surprised the founder?
opts: how much people valued the repair clinic
how quickly the membership fee was accepted
how difficult it was to explain borrowing
how few tools the church hall could hold
questions.expl: Ela diz que o empréstimo era fácil de explicar e que "What surprised me was the repair clinic". A alternativa sobre a dificuldade de explicar inverte o que ela afirma.

questions.text: In Text C, in the sentence "That is when they join", what does That refer to?
opts: the moment they repair something themselves
the moment they borrow their first tool
the moment the building was opened
the moment they hear about the library
questions.expl: A frase inteira é "That is when they join — not when they borrow, but when they fix". O próprio período dá a resposta e descarta o empréstimo.

questions.text: What does Text C suggest about how a new tool library should begin?
opts: on a small scale, with whatever space is available
with a purpose-built building from the start
with at least 1,200 tools in stock
only after a technician has been hired
questions.expl: O conselho dela é "Start with the shelf you already have", e ela conta que começaram com quarenta ferramentas num salão de igreja, com o prédio vindo depois.

questions.text: A member wants to keep a ladder for a second week. According to the three texts, this is possible if
opts: nobody is on the waiting list for it
the member pays an additional fee
the request is made at the counter
the ladder is returned to the repair clinic first
questions.expl: O texto B responde: renovar é possível "provided nobody is waiting for it", e itens na lista de espera não podem ser renovados. A renovação é online, não no balcão.

texts.html:
The Night Shift: photographs of a city that does not sleep

Municipal Gallery · 3 March – 28 May

For two years the photographer Ilan Serra followed the people whose working day begins when everyone else's ends: bakers, nurses, cleaners, port workers. The result is ninety black-and-white portraits, none of them posed.

  • Free entry on Wednesdays
  • Guided tours Saturdays at 11 a.m. (booking essential)
  • Not recommended for children under 10

An accompanying book is available at the gallery shop.

From the exhibition catalogue

Serra's decision to work only in black and white has been read as nostalgia, and he rejects the reading. Colour, he argues, would have told the viewer what time of night it was, and the point of the series is that the people in it have lost that information themselves. A nurse at four in the morning and a baker at four in the morning inhabit the same hour differently.

The absence of posing is equally deliberate. Serra spent the first months of each shift photographing nothing at all, on the grounds that a camera stops being an event only after it has been ignored several times. Critics who describe the portraits as candid are half right: they are unposed, but they were not taken by surprise.

Letters to the gallery

I worked nights in a hospital laundry for eleven years and I have never seen that work in a gallery before. My daughter came with me and asked why nobody was smiling. I told her they were, but not for the camera. — R. Mendes

The guided tour was excellent, though I would gently suggest that eleven in the morning is a cruel hour for an exhibition about people who sleep then. Could a late tour be added? — K. Abara

I came for the photographs and left thinking about the captions. Each one gives the person's name and trade and nothing else — no age, no story. It took me a room and a half to realise that this was the argument, not an omission. — T. Villar

questions.text: According to Text A, what is required to join a guided tour?
opts: a booking in advance
an entry fee on Wednesdays
the purchase of the exhibition book
a child under the age of ten
questions.expl: O texto A traz "Guided tours Saturdays at 11 a.m. (booking essential)". A entrada gratuita de quarta e o livro são outras informações da mesma lista.

questions.text: Why does the author of Text B mention a nurse and a baker?
opts: to show that the same hour is experienced in different ways
to explain which trades the photographer preferred
to argue that night work is harder in hospitals than in bakeries
to describe the two portraits that open the exhibition
questions.expl: A frase é "A nurse at four in the morning and a baker at four in the morning inhabit the same hour differently". Os dois são exemplos de uma mesma hora vivida de modos distintos.

questions.text: According to Text B, why did Serra work in black and white?
opts: because colour would have revealed the time of night
because black and white was cheaper to print
because the gallery asked for a uniform series
because he wanted the series to look nostalgic
questions.expl: O texto diz que a cor "would have told the viewer what time of night it was", e registra que ele REJEITA a leitura nostálgica — que é justamente a alternativa oposta.

questions.text: In Text B, which phrase is closest in meaning to candid?
opts: taken without the subject posing
printed without any editing
photographed from a long distance
published without permission
questions.expl: A própria frase esclarece: "they are unposed, but they were not taken by surprise". O crítico acerta a parte de não haver pose.

questions.text: What does Text B suggest about Serra's first months on each shift?
opts: They were spent making the workers used to his presence.
They produced the strongest images of the series.
They were required by the hospitals and bakeries.
They were used to test different kinds of film.
questions.expl: Ele passou os primeiros meses "photographing nothing at all", porque a câmera só deixa de ser um acontecimento depois de ser ignorada várias vezes. O objetivo era o hábito, não a imagem.

questions.text: In Text C, what does R. Mendes say about the people in the photographs?
opts: They were smiling, but not for the camera.
They were too tired to be photographed.
They had all worked in a hospital laundry.
They were posed by the photographer.
questions.expl: A carta responde à pergunta da filha: "I told her they were, but not for the camera". A lavanderia é o trabalho de quem escreve, não o dos retratados.

questions.text: Why does K. Abara write to the gallery?
opts: to propose a tour at a more convenient time
to complain about the quality of the guided tour
to ask for a refund of the entry fee
to praise the captions used in the exhibition
questions.expl: Ela elogia a visita guiada e sugere que onze da manhã é hora cruel para quem dorme nesse horário, perguntando: "Could a late tour be added?".

questions.text: In Text C, in "this was the argument, not an omission", what does this refer to?
opts: giving only the name and trade in each caption
hanging the photographs in a single room
printing the series in black and white
leaving the exhibition without buying the book
questions.expl: A carta fala das legendas, que trazem "the person's name and trade and nothing else". É essa escolha que ele passou a ler como argumento, e não como falha.

questions.text: What do the three letters in Text C have in common?
opts: Each responds to a specific choice made by the exhibition.
Each asks the gallery to extend the exhibition.
Each was written by someone who works at night.
Each criticises the photographer's technique.
questions.expl: As três reagem a uma decisão concreta: a ausência de sorrisos posados, o horário da visita e as legendas. Só a primeira carta é de quem trabalhou à noite.

questions.text: Taken together, what do Texts A, B and C show about the exhibition?
opts: Its choices were deliberate and were noticed by visitors.
It was more popular with critics than with the public.
It was assembled quickly and with little planning.
It focused on a single profession in one hospital.
questions.expl: O texto A apresenta a exposição, o B explica as decisões do fotógrafo e o C mostra visitantes reagindo justamente a essas decisões. As outras alternativas contradizem os textos.
